intent: THE PERCH — small footprint, large presence

FRONT.criticism: Every plumbed room is pinned to the uphill band y23-32, and y=32 IS the exterior face. MECH/WATER ENTRY is a corner room with two exterior walls and holds the most freeze-critical pipe in the building. The claimed 26 lf of wet wall cannot be an interior line: the longest interior run is 24 ft; the only 26 ft dimension in the plate is the exterior side wall. Either the metric is wrong or the wet wall is an exterior wall - a direct violation of the stated freeze rule at 3,400 ft.

builder_log.text:
BUILD INTENT: THE PERCH — small footprint, large presence

OPERATION: Refuse the horizontal. One very small footprint, lifted clear of the ground, stacked vertically, with a single enormous opening on the downhill face and a shutter that closes the whole thing when nobody is there.

REFERENCE IT COMES FROM: Sol Duc Cabin (350 sf, lifted, one enormous opening, closes completely) and Vermont Cabin (750 sf, monumental for its size)

DO NOT COPY: The steel plate aesthetic and the hand-crank theatre. The transferable things are the tiny ground contact, the vertical stack, and resilience expressed as a STATE rather than as equipment in a closet.
THE TEST THIS SCHEME MUST PASS: On a 30% slope, does going up beat going along? And can a house this small still hold a family at Christmas?
Plan authored and machine-checked. 3 levels, 20 rooms accepted by tools/build-plans.mjs; 10 flags raised.
Built in 3D from that plan by tools/render/lib/build3d.mjs and rendered. 21 parts. 1,872 sf conditioned, 100 lf perimeter, 26 lf wet wall, 17 CY cut.

VERDICT LOSS. FATAL and MAJOR findings retained; MINOR findings on closets and laundry position omitted for length.

FATAL · MECH/WATER ENTRY x20 y23 4x9 (ffe 6); POWDER; LAUNDRY; BATH x24 y23 10x9 (ffe 16)
Every plumbed room is pinned to the uphill band y23-32, and y=32 IS the exterior face. MECH/WATER ENTRY is a corner room with two exterior walls and holds the most freeze-critical pipe in the building. The claimed 26 lf of wet wall cannot be an interior line: the longest interior run is 24 ft; the only 26 ft dimension in the plate is the exterior side wall. Either the metric is wrong or the wet wall is an exterior wall - a direct violation of the stated freeze rule at 3,400 ft.

FATAL · STAIR x34 y23 10x9 on all three floors; LOFT (bed) at ffe 26
One stair is the only vertical route and the only way out of a sleeping room 20 ft above the only exterior door. The house is lifted on a plinth on a 30% slope, so the loft's downhill sill is roughly 30-40 ft above downhill grade - beyond ground-ladder rescue, on a road a volunteer department reaches slowly in winter. A fire on ffe 6, which holds the kitchen, laundry and mechanical room, cuts off both bedroom floors at once.

FATAL · The shutter over the downhill opening at y=6; STORE/SHUTTER GEAR at ffe 26
One shutter closes the entire downhill face, which is the only glazing serving DINING, LIVING, BED 1, BED 2, LOFT and WORK. Closed, it blacks out every habitable room and covers the emergency escape opening of all three sleeping rooms simultaneously. The operating gear sits on the third floor behind the only stair. Nothing is drawn for interior manual release, per-floor override or fail-open - and at 3,400 ft it will ice up in whatever position it was last left.

MAJOR · BATH x24 y23 10x9 (ffe 16) - the only full bath; STORE/SHUTTER GEAR directly above it
Three sleeping rooms, a family, and one full bath, plus a powder two floors below it. Loft occupants descend a 10 ft flight at night to reach a toilet. The plan already has a perfectly aligned 10x9 wet stack - POWDER+LAUNDRY at ffe 6, BATH at ffe 16 - and at ffe 26 squanders it on shutter storage. The riser is already there and the plan declines to use it.

MAJOR · Whole of ffe 6 - no bed, no shower
There is no level on which a person who cannot climb stairs could live. A doctor with a broken ankle from this very slope, an ageing parent, a post-op recovery, a newborn: all locked out. The only bay stacking clear on all three floors that could take a future lift is 4 ft wide - short of a residential shaft - and occupied at the bottom by the water entry.

MAJOR · KITCHEN x20 y16 14x7
Seven feet nominal will not take a double-loaded kitchen. Subtract two partitions and the clear width is about 6'-2"; two 25 in. counters leave roughly 32 in. of aisle, under the 36 in. minimum and far under the 42-48 in. anyone actually cooks in. Single-loaded, 14 lf must hold range, sink, refrigerator, dishwasher and all prep in the primary kitchen of a family house.

MAJOR · KITCHEN and its y=23 wall shared with MECH, POWDER and LAUNDRY
The kitchen has no downhill exposure - the cook stands with their back to the view and the winter sun, the one thing this scheme exists to capture. Meanwhile the y=23 wall carries three service doors into food prep, including a WC door opening directly into the kitchen.

MAJOR · STAIR x34 y23 10x9, floor-to-floor 10 ft
The stair does not close in the box drawn. Ten feet at 7 in. risers is 17-18 risers and about 14'-2" of run; a switchback in a 10x9 box needs roughly 9'-8" in the 9 ft dimension. It is short, so something gives, and it will be winders - on the sole means of egress from two sleeping floors. No switchback at 3 ft flight width will pass a backboard. This is a doctor's house on a 30% icy slope.

MAJOR · BED 1 over KITCHEN; LOFT directly over BED 1; WORK directly over BED 2
The client sleeps at odd hours and takes call, and every room sits directly on an occupied room with the worst possible assignments: the primary bedroom's floor is the kitchen's ceiling, the loft bed is over the primary bed, and WORK is over BED 2. No buffer layer is used anywhere. The one explicitly stated program requirement is the one the plan structurally cannot meet.

MAJOR · MUD/GEAR x34 y16 10x7 - the only exterior door
One exterior door in the entire building, on the uphill face, at the same corner as the only stair. That door is where the cut bank sloughs and drifts, and a single roof plane dumps its whole snow load along one line: shed it uphill and it buries this door. The LAUNDRY and MECH - the two commonest ignition sources in a house - flank the only vertical escape route and the only exit.

MAJOR · GALLERY HALL x20 y19 24x4 at ffe 16 and 26
462 sf of circulation, 25% of a 1,872 sf house, from a plan that sells itself on efficiency. The 24 ft gallery is 4 ft wide with no daylight at either end, and exists only because the stair is parked in the far corner; at ffe 26 that 96 sf corridor is spent reaching a store room and a mechanical closet. A quarter of the interior given to getting around is roughly a whole bedroom and bath handed away.

SUCK 100 — Every plumbed room is pinned to the uphill band y23-32, and y=32 IS the exterior face. MECH/WATER ENTRY is a corner room with two exterior walls and holds the most freeze-critical pipe in the building. The claimed 26 lf of wet wall cannot be an interior line: the longest interior run is 24 ft; the only 26 ft dimension in the plate is the exterior side wall. Either the metric is wrong or the wet wall is an exterior wall - a direct violation of the stated freeze rule at 3,400 ft.
